title: Second-difference biextension and its doubled geometric Picard class
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field] and let $H$ be a smooth separated commutative finite-type $k$-group scheme with identity $e$, addition $m$, and inverse $\iota$ [def-pc-scheme, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. The group operations satisfy the commutative group identities, and separated means its diagonal is a closed immersion. Assume $H$ is geometrically semiabelian: over an algebraic closure $\bar k$, there is an exact sequence of fppf sheaves $1\to\mathbf G_{m,\bar k}^r\to H_{\bar k}\to A\to1$, with $r\geq0$, $\mathbf G_{m,\bar k}=\operatorname{Spec}\bar k[t,t^{-1}]$, and $A$ a proper smooth geometrically connected group scheme [def-weil-proper-morphism, def-weil-algebraic-closure]. Let $L$ be any invertible module on $H$ [def-sc-invertible-module], and choose a trivialization $r:e^*L\simeq k$. Put $D_2(L)=m^*L\otimes p_1^*L^{\vee}\otimes p_2^*L^{\vee}$ on $H\times_kH$, with axis trivializations induced by $r$, where $p_1,p_2$ are the projections and $L^\vee$ is the dual invertible module. A $\mathbf G_m$-biextension of two commutative $S$-group schemes $(P,Q)$ means an invertible module $E$ on $P\times_S Q$ [def-sc-invertible-module], with trivializations on both identity axes agreeing at their intersection and isomorphisms $E_{x+x',y}\simeq E_{x,y}\otimes E_{x',y}$ and $E_{x,y+y'}\simeq E_{x,y}\otimes E_{x,y'}$. These are isomorphisms of pulled-back invertible modules on $P\times_SP\times_SQ$ and $P\times_SQ\times_SQ$, respectively; they satisfy associativity, commutativity and the identity laws in each variable, and the interchange law saying that expanding $E_{x+x',y+y'}$ in either order gives the same map to the tensor product of its four factors. Isomorphisms of biextensions preserve both laws and both axis trivializations. Tensor and pullback are [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product, def-pc-module-pullback]. The invertible module $D_2(L)$ admits a biextension structure for $(H,H)$ with these axis trivializations. If $\Delta:H\to H\times_kH$ is the diagonal, then $\Delta^*D_2(L)\otimes(L^\vee)^{\otimes2}$ is geometrically algebraically trivial. Here geometric algebraic equivalence is the equivalence relation after extension to $\bar k$ generated by pairs of fibres of an invertible module on $H_{\bar k}\times T$, with $T$ a smooth connected $\bar k$-variety; geometrically algebraically trivial means equivalent to $\mathcal O$. Equivalently, the diagonal pullback has class $2[L]$ modulo this subgroup of $\operatorname{Pic}(H)$, the group of invertible-module isomorphism classes with tensor as addition. No symmetry, ampleness, perfectness of $k$, or splitting over $k$ is assumed.

proof.text: Work first over $\bar k$ with the extension in the hypothesis, denoting its quotient by $q:H_{\bar k}\to A$ and its kernel by $T=\mathbf G_m^r$. Exactness gives fppf local lifts of points of $A$; a lift $h$ identifies $T$ with its fibre by $t\mapsto h+t$, with inverse $h'\mapsto h'-h$. Thus the sheaf represented by $H_{\bar k}$ is a $T_A$-torsor. The torus is affine, smooth and finitely presented: its coordinate presentation has generators $t_i,u_i$ with $t_iu_i=1$, and units lift across first-order nilpotent thickenings. Apply [lem-sfb-smooth-affine-group-torsor-representability] to this torsor. Its represented morphism is $q$, so $q$ is affine, smooth, surjective and open. It is flat by [lem-pc-smooth-flat] and of finite presentation by [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation] (affine implies quasi-compact and quasi-separated). By [lem-sfb-split-torus-torsor-frame-geometry], it is a product of punctured invertible modules over $A$, hence Zariski locally the projection $U\times\mathbf G_m^r\to U$. Every fibre is connected, since a Laurent polynomial ring over a field is a domain. If $H_{\bar k}$ had a nontrivial clopen decomposition, the images of the two pieces under the open map $q$ would be disjoint nonempty opens covering connected $A$: a connected fibre cannot meet both pieces. This is impossible. Thus $H_{\bar k}$ is connected, so $H$ is geometrically connected over $k$ by [lem-weil-geometrically-connected-algebraic-closure]. The same quotient $q$ and its torsor properties will be used below.

proof.text: The base $\operatorname{Spec}k$ is normal and reduced: a field has no nonzero nilpotents and is its own fraction field. The smooth separated finite-type morphism $H\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is of finite presentation: smooth implies locally of finite presentation, finite type gives quasi-compactness, and separated gives quasi-separatedness, so the comparison clause of [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation] applies. Step 1 supplies geometric connectedness; the required semiabelian geometric fibre is precisely the hypothesis. Therefore [lem-sfb-semiabelian-cubical-rigidification], case (b), equips $(L,r)$ over $k$ with a cubical structure $\tau$ in the sense of [def-sfb-cubical-rigidified-line]. We use its normalized section $\mathcal O\simeq\Theta_3(L)$. No field extension or descent of this structure is needed.

source.place: Revised March 14, 2021 thesis, §§3.2.2–3.2.3, equations (3.2.2.3)–(3.2.2.4), Definition 3.2.2.6, Proposition 3.2.3.1; primary online PDF https://www.kwlan.org/articles/cpt-PEL-type-thesis-revision-dense.pdf (local copy WANTED). Agent line-module realization.

proof.text:
Write $E=D_2(L)$. Use the functorial tensor and composition comparisons of [lem-weil-pbc-invertible-pullback-tensor]; duals cancel by evaluation on a rank-one free local frame. On $H^3$, cancellation of the displayed factors identifies
$$E_{x+x',y}\otimes E_{x,y}^{-1}\otimes E_{x',y}^{-1}\simeq\Theta_3(L)_{x,x',y},$$
where the constant $e^*L$ factor on the right is trivialized by $r$. Explicitly the uncancelled factors on the left are $L_{x+x'+y}L_xL_{x'}L_y/(L_{x+x'}L_{x+y}L_{x'+y})$, exactly the definition of $\Theta_3(L)$ in [def-sfb-cubical-rigidified-line] after that normalization. Applying $\tau^{-1}$ gives an isomorphism $\alpha:E_{x+x',y}\simeq E_{x,y}\otimes E_{x',y}$. Permuting the three variables gives $\beta:E_{x,y+y'}\simeq E_{x,y}\otimes E_{x,y'}$. These are global isomorphisms of pulled-back invertible modules, not fibrewise choices. When any of the three variables is $e$, the unit-face condition on $\tau$ makes these maps the canonical cancellation maps for the axis trivializations induced by $r$. At $(e,e)$ both axes give the same trivialization of $(e^*L)^{-1}$.

source.place: Revised March 14, 2021 thesis, §§3.2.2–3.2.3, equations (3.2.2.3)–(3.2.2.4), Definition 3.2.2.6, Proposition 3.2.3.1; primary online PDF https://www.kwlan.org/articles/cpt-PEL-type-thesis-revision-dense.pdf (local copy WANTED). Agent line-module realization.

proof.text: Here is a direct coherence check for these laws. For associativity in the first variable, compare $(\alpha_{x,x',y}\otimes1)\alpha_{x+x',x'',y}$ and $(1\otimes\alpha_{x',x'',y})\alpha_{x,x'+x'',y}$ on $H^4$. They have the same source and target after the canonical tensor reorderings. Their ratio is a global unit, since an automorphism of an invertible module is scalar multiplication (check a free rank-one local frame). On each of the four coordinate axes it is 1: if only $y$ varies all first-variable arguments are $e$, and if only one first-variable argument varies then $y=e$; in either case all maps are the normalized cancellation maps of step 3. The last assertion of [lem-sfb-relative-group-unit-axis-factorization], applied to $H$ with $n=4$ over the reduced field base, makes this unit 1. Interchanging the variables proves associativity for $\beta$. The commutativity defects of $\alpha$ and $\beta$ are units on $H^3$, equal to 1 on its axes by the same unit-face calculation; apply that statement with $n=3$. Finally the two expansions of $E_{x+x',y+y'}$ have common target $E_{x,y}\otimes E_{x',y}\otimes E_{x,y'}\otimes E_{x',y'}$. Their ratio is a unit on $H^4$. On any coordinate axis at most one variable is nonidentity, so every occurrence of a partial law reduces to the cancellation map and both composites agree. Apply the same assertion with $n=4$. The identity laws were already checked in step 3. Thus $E$, with $\alpha,\beta$ and the prescribed axes, is a biextension over $k$.

proof.text: For the remaining assertion it suffices, by its definition, to work over $\bar k$. The abelian quotient $A$ in step 1 is smooth, proper and connected, hence an abelian variety [def-sc-abelian-variety]; it is separated and of finite type because it is proper. The morphism $q$ is a split-torus torsor with all the hypotheses verified in step 1. Apply [lem-sfb-split-torus-torsor-line-pullback] with $X=A$ and $Y=H_{\bar k}$ to obtain an invertible module $N$ on $A$ and an isomorphism $L_{\bar k}\simeq q^*N$. Only surjectivity on line-module classes is used; neither $N$ nor this isomorphism must descend to $k$.

source.place: Chapter I §10, Remark 10.19, printed p.50; agent pullback along the split-torus quotient.

proof.text:
Since $m\Delta=[2]_H$ and $p_i\Delta=1_H$, the tensor comparisons of [lem-weil-pbc-invertible-pullback-tensor] give
$$\Delta^*D_2(L)\otimes(L^\vee)^{\otimes2}\simeq[2]_H^*L\otimes(L^\vee)^{\otimes4}.$$
Over $\bar k$, use $q[2]_H=[2]_Aq$ and step 5 to identify this with
$$q^*\bigl([2]_A^*N\otimes(N^\vee)^{\otimes4}\bigr).$$
By [lem-sfb-abelian-multiplication-algebraic-equivalence] with $n=2$, the line inside parentheses is algebraically trivial; that lemma imposes no symmetry or characteristic restriction. Pullback preserves the specified equivalence relation directly: a generating family $F$ on $A\times T$ pulls back to $(q\times1_T)^*F$ on $H_{\bar k}\times T$, with the same smooth connected parameter $T$ and the prescribed two pulled-back fibres, by the composition comparison. Pull back each family in a chain from this line to $\mathcal O_A$. This proves geometric algebraic triviality of the displayed line on $H$, and therefore $[\Delta^*D_2(L)]=2[L]$ in the asserted quotient.
